about.title: Chino Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: A work injury in Chino rarely stays at work. It follows you home to the mortgage, the school pickups, and the question of whether the paycheck keeps coming. Workers' compensation is the starting point for most people employed in San Bernardino County, and it applies no matter who was at fault. But it also limits what you can recover from your employer, and it says nothing about pain or the full weight of what you lost. That gap matters when someone other than your employer contributed to the harm: a subcontractor on a job site, a property owner who ignored a hazard, a manufacturer whose equipment failed, or a driver who hit you while you were on the clock along Central Avenue or Riverside Drive. Chino recorded 400 injury collisions in 2025, with 571 people hurt, and some of those involved someone simply doing their job. We can review your case at no charge to help you understand which claims exist and which may be worth pursuing.

items.title: Two Paths, Reviewed Together
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your only remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party can open a separate injury claim. We look at both instead of assuming comp is the end of the story.

items.title: Deadlines Kept Straight
items.desc: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and third-party claims carry a two-year deadline. Getting in touch early means neither clock catches you off guard.

items.title: Protection From Pushback
items.desc: Retaliation for reporting an injury or filing a claim is illegal in California. If your hours were cut or your job threatened after you spoke up, that belongs in the conversation too.

items.question: I was rear-ended on the SR-60 while making deliveries for my employer. Is that workers' comp or a car accident claim?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' comp should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of fault. Separately, the other driver is a third party, so you may also have an injury claim against them within the two-year deadline. Chino's collisions cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., which is exactly when many delivery and commute shifts overlap.

items.question: Do I really have to report the injury to my employer within 30 days?
items.answer: Yes, and sooner is better. California expects notice within 30 days, and delays can complicate your comp benefits. Put it in writing if you can, keep a copy, and note who you told and when. Reporting is also what makes any later retaliation easier to prove.

items.question: Do you charge me anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. Our team provides a free case review. We work on contingency, which means no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
